sampledSpectrum.source: Gaia Collaboration (2023), Gaia Data Release 3, A&A 674, A1; BP/RP spectra: De Angeli et al. (2023), A&A 674, A2; external calibration: Montegriffo et al. (2023), A&A 674, A3
sampledSpectrum.service: Sampled here from the continuous product, photometry/gaia-dr3-xp-continuous.csv (https://gea.esac.esa.int/data-server/data?RETRIEVAL_TYPE=XP_CONTINUOUS&ID=Gaia+DR3+2635476908753563008&format=csv&DATA_STRUCTURE=RAW), with GaiaXPy's calibrate on the archive's own 336-1020 nm grid: tools/objects/observation/xp-continuous-sample.py. Gaia publishes sampled spectra only for brighter sources; at G = 15.62 this star has the coefficients only.
sampledSpectrum.sampling: 343 samples from 336 to 1020 nm in 2 nm steps, flux in W m^-2 nm^-1 (the DataLink default sampling)
sampledSpectrum.note: Gaia's own low-resolution spectrum of the star, calibrated to absolute flux. Its samples at the even wavelengths from 380 to 780 nm are weighted by the CIE 1931 2-degree observer. This star is a cool dwarf: below about 450 nm its samples scatter around zero (mean signal-to-noise 0.2 from 380 to 450 nm), and a sample that is negative within its own error is read as no emission at that wavelength. The range in the prepared report is the colour of the spectrum moved one standard error down and up at every sample, which is wide in blue for the same reason.
